messages:
maya: Customer reports streaming sessions that silently stop sending tokens after ~40s, client then reconnects repeatedly and sees partial JSON chunks. They say billing shows multiple short responses for a single user action.

chris: Do we have a request_id / example session id? Also which fronting proxy (ALB / CF / GCLB)?

maya: Request id 01GZQ2X5, hitting ALB in us-west-2. Customer attached a Chrome network capture and logs. Quick repro they gave:

maya: ```bash
curl -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-streamer
```

maya: Client shows event stream data, then a few seconds of no bytes, then TCP RST and reconnect. Partial payload ends with "choices":[{"delta":{"content":"The answer is"}} (no final completion).

noah: ALB idle timeout is 60s by default. If client isn't receiving anything and nothing is sent from server, ALB can close. TCP keepalive is OS-level, but many public proxies ignore it.

eli: Agreed. Also see cases where intermediate proxies collapse connections if there's long silence. Two options: server-side comment pings (SSE comment lines like `: ping\n\n`) every 15-30s OR change ALB idle to >120s (not always customer-controllable).

chris: Two engineering tradeoffs: 1) comment pings preserve stream and are free from a token accounting perspective (they are bytes on the wire but not model tokens), 2) server can also send small whitespace chunks which some clients treat oddly. Need to ensure SDKs ignore comment events.

maya: Customer also reported auth churn: their short-lived token was expiring and on reconnect we return 401 which creates a loop and duplicates billing entries.

chris: Important. On reconnect we should attempt to match Last-Event-ID and dedupe server-side until the new auth is accepted. Also recommend client use refresh token flow so reconnects don't get 401.

noah: Proposed immediate mitigation for support: ask customer to enable SSE comment pings from client or increase ALB idle. Repro steps for them to try:

noah: 1) Run curl with `-N` as above. 2) After stream start, run `nc -vz <client-ip> 443` to observe RST? (optional). 3) Add periodic SSE comment sender (server) `echo ": ping"` every 20s.

eli: Example server-side comment heartbeat snippet (node):

eli: ```js
// after SSE headers sent
setInterval(() => { res.write(': hb\n\n'); }, 20000);
// server idle enforcement
const IDLE_MAX_MS = 120000; // drop after 2m
```

chris: SDK changes: ensure the JS/py streaming client treats lines starting with `:` as keepalive, does not convert to events, and doesn't count them as messages. Add an option `heartbeat_interval_ms` default 0 (off) to clients so we don't break existing flows.

maya: For billing side: ops, can we confirm whether keepalive comments are currently billed as tokens? Customer emphasizes cost.

eli: Comments are raw bytes and do not get tokenized by the model, so they should not count as model tokens. But they do appear in request/response byte metrics — I'll flag billing metrics team to confirm there are no edge cases.

support-bot: Ticket #53721 created, linked to 01GZQ2X5, priority P2. Assigned to @chris for runtime changes and @eli for infra mitigations.

chris: Short-term action items:
- Ask customer to enable server or client comment pings (20s) or increase ALB idle.
- Add Last-Event-ID tolerant reconnection path to dedupe outputs on reconnect.
- Track auth-refresh guidance to prevent 401 on reconnect.

maya: I'll send the customer a suggested repro script and the heartbeat snippet now.

noah: Long-term: add automated detection in console that flags streams which have no data for >45s and suggests heartbeat or config changes. Also add a SLO: detect >3 reconnects within 2m and surface as incident.

chris: Sounds good. I'll open a runtime PR with comment-ping support and a feature flag for 2 weeks, then we can roll it to all streaming endpoints.

maya: Thanks team. Customer awaiting steps; sending them the snippet and the ticket link. :thumbsup:
